goal_title: Book: Isosurfaces: Implicit to Explicit — improvements from the spine reading
why: The whole spine was read as a book on 2026-09-24, one sequence at a time, and every stumble, false claim or broken handover in isosurfaces became a task Palle can pick up one at a time. Reader: the VR visitor.
success_criteria: every open task here is done or skipped with a note
the chapters read through without a stumble in the headset
every code excerpt and number in the chapters matches the source

reading.arc: The sequence takes one idea, a field of values cut at a chosen level, and walks it from a wireframe specimen to a building the visitor stands inside. The first seven halls each put a six-button desk beside an existing GPU field: the intro's LEVEL/SAMPLES, the fifteen-case MARGIN, the gallery's REPERTOIRE/LEVEL, the gyroid's PERIOD/INTRUSION/PROBE, the sculptor's PAIR/ADD/ERASE, the terrain's INTERIOR/TERMS/COLUMN, the portal's TERMS, and every desk has HOLD, which leaves a collisionless copy for comparison. The line of argument is that the same extractor serves different descriptions (chair, cup, gyroid, hand strokes, height fields, composed terms), and that boundary, enclosed volume and passage are three different questions. After ISO_Caves the halls lose their desks and shorten to 330-430 words: cave generation as authored distribution, animated noise as replacement rather than motion, metaballs as a sum crossing a threshold, raymarching as display without triangles, and the rhizome body as a graph with cycles turned into a shell you can enter. The close is right (a connection has to fit a body) but the last five chapters end in 'a useful extension would', describing instruments the rooms do not have.
holds: HOLD: eight of nine desks leave a held copy behind or beside the live specimen, always 'display copy, no collision'. The held-versus-live comparison is the sequence's carried method and its recurring object.

The refrain that a visible opening is not clearance for a body: intro (hole vs clearance), gyroid (the capsule probe and 'an untested wall must not become evidence of freedom'), terrain (the column counter 'does not decide'), portal, caves ('a counter is not a body'), rhizome ('a connection has to fit a body').

A name is an intention, the field makes the surface: Cup and Chair in the gallery, 'formula' on the gyroid desk, 'arched' on the terrain and portal desks, 'portal' in the caves, 'entropy' in the hall before.

The sampling budget as a standing number: 24/16/32 in the intro, then 64 per axis in the gallery, gyroid, sculptor and portal readouts, so 'a narrow feature can be absent from the mesh while present in its formula' recurs with a figure attached.
The desk grammar itself: 'Press X', a readout line, a RULE card, RESET that keeps the held copy. By the fourth hall the reader knows the instrument before reading the room.

Level as the movable line: 0.50/0.45/0.55 in the intro, 0.50 fixed while MARGIN moves the crossing, 0/-2/+4/+10 in the gallery, level one on the gyroid, level zero for the sculptor, the shell's wall in the rhizome.

hall_notes.note: The noise field as a blue specimen with pink triangle edges; LEVEL 0.50/0.45/0.55, SAMPLES 24/16/32 (13,824/4,096/32,768), HOLD to the right, 0.18 scale making 5.76 m. Every number and both code lines check against VoxelNoiseMarchingCubes.gd and iso_workshop.gd. Reads calmly and sets the three-question refrain (boundary, volume, passage).

The fifteen-case rack; MARGIN moves the values 0.30/0.70 to 0.14/0.54, 0.44/0.84, 0.48/0.88 and the crossing 0.50, 0.10, 0.85, 0.95 with masks fixed; TRACE's gold markers; arrangement 1 = table mask 254. Exact throughout and the 'which view invites you to forget the construction' question is the hall's best line. Says nothing about the Threshold Opinion standing nine cells further on.

Chair and cup; HOLD copies the middle-column pair; LEVEL 0 to -2 to +4 to +10 over all six fields; the cup as min(max(-inside, outside), handle); REPERTOIRE household/laboratory/abstract/survey; the cup vanishing at -2 with its labelled place left empty. The best-argued gallery hall; the close about escaping a name is a keeper.

Longest chapter. Torus at 'formula' (weights zero), gyroid with PERIOD 0.5/1/2/4 and INTRUSION erosion, modulation, warp; the quoted shader line is verbatim; the PROBE capsule (0.20/0.35/0.60 m, 1.70 m tall, 12 m rail) is the sequence's first honest clearance test and the chapter is careful about what it does not prove. Dense but every device earns its place.

Two deposits 0.90/0.65/0.45 m apart, radius 0.30; ADD/ERASE at a gold target with a quarter-metre brush; the cut as max(field, -brush); order as part of the form; the 500-edit memory. Strong lesson, but it carries 'In VR,' and a sentence of repair history the reader cannot use.

Turquoise height field with INTERIOR 0/0.3/0.4/0.8 and the 25x25 COLUMN counter; amber composed field with TERMS. Keeps the two experiments apart ('not a matched pair differing by one switch'), the code matches MarchingCubesFlat.glsl and the overhang shader, and the closing note honestly points at the CPU terrain and rhizome at the back.

The composed field with TERMS hillside to compound and a held bay of matching scale; fine sentences on names arriving before features and on a copy entering 'with different permissions'. But its one work is the same scene the reader just drove as the amber specimen next door, and the chapter presents it as a new landscape.

PORTALS 1/3/7/16 and BURIAL, the enclosing cave's PLUMB and OCTAVES 1/2/3/6, HOLD behind the cave; the queer cave gets two sentences. The closing four lines are the sequence's thesis. The enclosure claim ('above, beside and behind the eye') rests on a 2 %-scale bay token and a desktop-rig review, not a headset walk.

No desk. Compares this cave with the enclosing one and is honest that noise scale 13.5 vs 3.8, level 0.85 vs 0.88 and extent 300 vs 280 all changed at once. Silent about the second specimen on its stage, which is a hand-written sine tunnel, and it ends in an extension addressed to 'visitors'.

Replacement versus travel; correctly calls the blocks boundary-containing cells rather than a mesh (the extractor really emits whole cubes) and names the trig field and the 0.2 s rebuild. No desk; the mc_base tunnel beside the block set is unmentioned; ends in an extension.

Shortest hall. EMPLACE column/ring/pair/shell/scatter and KERNEL inverse square/Wyvill/Gaussian/cone over ten sources, HOLD behind. Three one-line regions for the secondary works; the 'small rear specimen' is the largest body in the room and the code block is pseudo-code fenced as gdscript.

Explains the ray march well (bounded steps and a finite tolerance are both in the shader: 80 steps, 0.001) and keeps display and collision apart. But it opens as a first meeting with a body the reader passed at the back of ISO_Caves and twice in ISO_Metaballs, and never says this placement's joins are set to 'necked'.

The plan as a graph with cycles, the shell, cut entrances, mesh and collision chunks: all of it is in rhizome_inside.gd (Kruskal tree plus extra edges, connectivity assert, abs(field) - wall). Asks the reader for a loop and distinguishes a planned cycle from a demonstrated return. A fitting close; the one hall where a two-line code excerpt is missing and would land.

stumbles: ISO_PortalLandscape: the reader has just pressed TERMS on this exact scene as the amber specimen in ISO_FlatTerrain; 'The landscape begins with hills' reads as a new object and the same glsl block is quoted twice.

ISO_Caves: 'The portal landscape is a promise made by a boundary' arrives one hall after Portal Landscape, whose chapter insisted its specimen was not a portal and had no rings; the reader must work out that a second, ringed portal landscape is meant.
ISO_Metaballs: 'The small rear specimen' is the same raymarched scene as 'the raymarched specimen nearby', standing at scale 1 (a 12 m box) against the nearby one's 0.2.

ISO_ImplicitModeling: 'Must a surface exist as a triangle mesh before you can see it?' was answered in one sentence in the previous hall, about the same body, which the reader has now met three times.

ISO_CaveGeneration: 'Compare this cave specimen with the one you have just inspected' and 'Both specimens' are ambiguous on a stage that holds two specimens, one of which is a striped stand-in tunnel and not a field.
ISO_Sculpting: 'In VR, move a controller' implies the reader might not be in the headset; the next paragraph's 'earlier implementation accidentally' sentence is a changelog.
ISO_Caves: 'A column can show several crossings, but a counter is not a body' sends the reader looking for a COLUMN readout that is two halls back.

ISO_LookupTable: the closing handover repeats 'description' three times, and the Threshold Opinion (five surfaces from one field, a resolution row, a brass rack of the fifteen) stands in the hall with no text.

ISO_CaveGeneration, ISO_AnimatedNoise, ISO_ImplicitModeling, ISO_RhizomeBody: four consecutive halls end in 'A useful extension would', addressed once to 'visitors', describing instruments the reader cannot press.

keep.quote: What matters is remembering that a smooth-looking silhouette at a distance does not erase the finite pieces from which this display is made.

Absence from the mesh does not establish absence from the underlying field, particularly where a feature falls between widely separated samples. Nor does a visible hole establish clearance for your body.
Which view lets you explain what just happened, and which invites you to forget the construction?
The cup need not remain a cup. But escaping its name will take more than changing the label.
If the generator omitted collision because the mesh was too costly, the desk says the probe is unavailable; an untested wall must not become evidence of freedom.
This instrument's memory helps make the body, and also decides what it can cease to remember.
Some changes are small; a new word on the desk can arrive more dramatically than a new feature in the surface.

A portal can be a hole that does not connect; an enclosing cave can be a room with no adequate entrance. The field supplies possibilities. A route is authored through width, collision and a body that can arrive.

reading.handover_in: Clean. Topology_Entropy_Morphogenesis closes softbodies on a sampled surface with LEVEL, NOISE and RESOLUTION controls and the line 'a body has become a set of relations'. ISO_Introduction picks it up by name ('The porous specimen in the previous room introduced the same distinction between values and visible form') and its own LEVEL/SAMPLES desk reads as a continuation of those controls rather than a restart. Nothing in the intro contradicts the morphogenesis hall.
reading.handover_out: Clean and deliberate. ISO_RhizomeBody ends by naming union, intersection and difference and reminding the reader they have met their consequences in joined chambers, wall shells and cut entrances; Boolean_Verbs opens on a box and a sphere and explicitly contrasts CSG with what came before ('Earlier, distance fields let a parameter round the meeting between forms. Here there is no smoothing band') and repeats the sequence's refrain that these exhibits have no collision. The only wrinkle is on the receiving side: Boolean_Verbs has no H1 title where every isosurfaces chapter does.

Cut the duplicated glsl block (keep it in FlatTerrain) and spend those lines on what the second pass shows.

tasks.title: Name nakama's limit: it never extracts a surface, so no neck can pinch off
tasks.spec:
[prose] ISO_Metaballs
Quote: “Nakama keeps the blob vocabulary but changes the implementation and the limits of the body. It is a comparison, not a third control on the desk.”
Why: The limit is specific and is this desk's lesson in negative: nakama extracts no isosurface at all, it pushes one sphere mesh in and out along its normals by (field minus threshold) times 0.2, so its body is pinned at genus 0 and can never show the neck pinching off that EMPLACE is there to produce.
Do: 'Nakama keeps the blob vocabulary but never extracts a surface: it pushes one sphere in and out by the field's value, so the body can breathe but no neck can ever pinch off. That is the comparison.'
